title: Buildings as Habitat: Adaptive Investments in Public Health

findings.antecedent: Hard-edged glass and concrete-dominated built environments
findings.consequent: Biodiversity loss (e.g., 1 billion songbirds killed annually in US)
findings.quote: Buildings kill an estimated 1 billion songbirds each year in the United States alone. Apart from the heartbreaking destruction of beautiful, innocent life, this catastrophic loss of biodiversity represents a public health emergency that tragically illuminates an all too literal clash between nature and culture.

findings.antecedent: Hard-edged glass and concrete-dominated built environments
findings.consequent: Human inflammatory conditions and degraded public health/well-being
findings.quote: As the pervasiveness of human inflammatory conditions suggests, our hard-edged glass and concrete-dominated environments do not support our own biology either.

findings.antecedent: Chronic stress from extreme heat, noise, light, and air pollution
findings.consequent: Degraded public health and well-being (loneliness, anxiety, dementia, hypertension, cancer, eroded immune response, reduced productivity, frayed social fabric)
findings.quote: In addition to biodiversity loss, chronic stress from extreme heat, noise, light, and air pollution degrades public health and well-being in many of our neighborhoods. From loneliness and anxiety to dementia, from hypertension to cancer, daily stress conditions erode our immune response, reduce productivity, and fray our social fabric.

findings.antecedent: Mismatch between ancient genes and modern building habits
findings.consequent: Physiological and neurological degradation
findings.quote: must we not also extend our care and efforts to protect the public from buildings that are physiologically and neurologically degrading because they represent “a mismatch between our ancient genes and our modern building habits.”

findings.antecedent: Removal from physiologically nourishing place ingredients (nature)
findings.consequent: Increased separation anxiety
findings.quote: It stands to reason that the further we remove ourselves from environments that integrate the physiologically nourishing place ingredients we evolved in and with, the more separation anxiety we seem to experience.

findings.consequent: Chronic stress and inflammatory conditions
findings.quote: evidence suggests that nature-negative built environments contribute significantly to the problem of chronic stress, the health consequences of which are not currently covered by construction warranties.

findings.antecedent: Cognitive dualism in built environments (disconnect from embodied animal nature)
findings.consequent: Neurobiologically mismatched places and cognitive dissonance
findings.quote: we have enshrined the paradigm of cognitive dualism in built environments that are profoundly out of step, and quite literally out of touch, with our embodied animal nature, creating neurobiologically mismatched places that generate in us something akin to cognitive dissonance.

findings.consequent: Chronic stress with public health consequences (anxiety, depression, dementia, hypertension, heart attacks, death)
key_citations: Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (OASH), 2023
findings.quote: US Surgeon General Dr. Vivek Murthy establishes as fact that loneliness and isolation represent a form of chronic stress with public health consequences akin to smoking, ranging from anxiety and depression to dementia, hypertension, heart attacks, and even death.

findings.consequent: Increased 'species' loneliness and decreased restoration
findings.quote: A related kind of loneliness afflicts us in places that are devoid of living nature... Richard Louv and others refer to it as “species' loneliness.”

findings.consequent: Decreased microbial gut diversity and increased inflammatory diseases (especially in children)
findings.quote: Residents of areas burdened by low biodiversity are more likely to suffer from decreased microbial gut diversity, which, especially in children, is “a key factor in determining disease susceptibility patterns later in life”

findings.antecedent: Extreme urban heat (due to mechanical systems, heat-absorbing materials, lack of natural cooling)
findings.consequent: Increased deaths, blackouts, and health risks for humans and birds
key_citations: Extreme heat: The economic and Social consequences for the United States, 2021
findings.quote: As extended extreme heat periods multiply, soaring mechanical air conditioning usage... creates a perilous cycle... Without adaptative measures, deaths from extreme heat... could increase by more than six times in the United States.

findings.consequent: Inflammatory respiratory conditions, systemic inflammation, cardiac/placental damage, decreased cognition, dementia, depression, antibiotic resistance
key_citations: Air Pollution may increase risk for dementia, 2023
Association between particulate matter (PM)2·5 air pollution and clinical antibiotic resistance: a global analysis, 2023
findings.quote: Human exposure to PM2.5 has been linked to inflammatory respiratory conditions, including lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, and interstitial lung damage... can trigger a systemic inflammatory response, affecting tissues and organs as well as causing blood clots and cardiac and placental damage.

findings.antecedent: Blue-white LED lighting (4000-5000 Kelvin) at night
findings.consequent: Circadian disruption, suppressed melatonin, hormonal dysregulation, diabetes, heart disease, obesity, depression, premature cell aging, dementia, cancer, impaired impulse control
findings.quote: Blue-white LED bulbs of 4000-5000 Kelvin customarily used in streetlights turn night into day. The detrimental health consequences they cause are now well understood. Our ancient body-brain associates these color temperature ranges with morning and floods the body with adrenaline and cortisol, increasing heart rate and generally marshaling energy resources for the demands of the day, except it is midnight. Melatonin, the sleep hormone essential for healthy immune system activity, is suppressed.

findings.consequent: Interference with internal magnetic orientation and increased deaths for night-migrating birds
findings.quote: The glare of our cities and electromagnetic radiation at close range interfere with their internal magnetic orientation mechanism, and the beacon effect of our night-illuminated glass towers lures tens of thousands of night-migrating birds to their deaths.

findings.consequent: Disrupted cardiovascular homeostasis, heart disease, stroke, metabolic disturbances, psychological disorders, premature morbidity, impaired learning/cognition, reduced creativity
findings.quote: the corrosive impact of chronic noise on cardiovascular homeostasis does not appear to require cognitive perception... Even at low decibel levels, persistent noise is a public health hazard, disrupting sleep and contributing to heart disease, stroke, metabolic disturbances, the escalation of psychological disorders and premature morbidity.

findings.consequent: Increased hearing loss, social isolation, depression, neurogenerative diseases (Alzheimer's, Parkinson's)
key_citations: Noise as a public health hazard, 2022
findings.quote: associated with a higher risk of hearing loss, which in turn increases the likelihood of social isolation and depression - see also loneliness as a stressor above - and possibly of neurogenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's' and Parkinson's Disease.

findings.antecedent: Built environments that keep ancient body-brain in chronic overstimulation
findings.consequent: Crisis-level physiological energy expenditures, reduced ability for nurture, care, love, social bonding, imagination, planning, play, learning
findings.quote: A great many of our built environments seem to keep our ancient body-brain in a state of chronic overstimulation, requiring crisis-level physiological energy expenditures on a daily basis.

findings.antecedent: Physiologically restorative place ingredients (e.g., 'vacation places' like leafy groves, meadows, flowing water, vibrant plant life)
findings.consequent: Reduced heart rate, raised vagal tone, activated NK cells, restored cognition, lifted mood, optimized physiological energy management
findings.quote: Place patterns and place ingredients that engage that 'vacation place feeling' reduce our heart rate, raise vagal tone, activate NK cells, restore our cognition, and lift our mood.

findings.antecedent: Engaged (soft, permeable) edge conditions (Ecotonal Building Envelopes)
findings.consequent: Reduced heart rate, increased physiological energy conservation, enhanced refuge & prospect, improved personal safety and community
findings.quote: Places with 'soft' edges are neurologically legible. More likely than not, they support a reduction in our heart rate because they simultaneously address our need for refuge & prospect (Appleton, 1975), personal safety, and community (also related to safety).

findings.antecedent: Ecotonal Building Envelopes (EBEs) / Vertical Greening Systems (VGS)
findings.consequent: Mitigated air, noise, and light pollution; naturally cooled interiors and neighborhoods; sequestered carbon; fostered urban micro-habitat biodiversity; enhanced well-being
findings.quote: Clothed in verdant Ecotonal Building Envelopes (EBEs), formerly hard-edged buildings are transformed into soft and vibrant places, alive with place ingredients offering enhanced well-being conditions that mitigate air, noise, and light pollution, naturally cool interiors as well as surrounding neighborhoods, and foster micro-habitat biodiversity in symbiotic realignment with the biology of all urban lives.

findings.consequent: Engaged parasympathetic nervous system, supported vagus nerve, released oxytocin, reduced inflammatory cytokines, strengthened immune response, increased cooperation and generosity
findings.quote: Keltner found that awe experiences engage the parasympathetic nervous system, support the vagus nerve, and release oxytocin, thus reducing inflammatory cytokines... Awe experiences are homeostatically effective via involuntary attention & soft fascination, key components of Attention Restoration Theory (ART).

findings.consequent: Improved cognitive function
findings.quote: As Kate E. Lee's research of 'micro-breaks' suggests, mere 40-second views of nature have the power to improve cognitive function.

findings.consequent: Enhanced immune regulation, preventative health benefits, rewilded urban microbial processes
findings.quote: restoring urban biodiversity provides a low-risk and low-cost investment that is likely to rewild urban microbial processes and have potential to pay generational health dividends. We believe that these restoration investments are imperative for tackling the ongoing decline in urban green spaces, rapid growth in urban populations, and increases in microbially-mediated non-communicable diseases.

findings.consequent: Reduced ambient temperature near facade (up to 7°C/12.6°F cooler), improved energy efficiency, mitigated urban heat islands
findings.quote: Experimental studies reveal that using plants as part of the building envelope significantly reduces ambient temperature close to the facade as well as interior temperatures, materially improving energy efficiency... The temperature of building façades shaded by VGS was shown to be up to 7°C (12.6°F) cooler than ambient air, thereby also positively affecting neighboring buildings by reducing heat reflection.

findings.consequent: Reduced NO2 and PM10 concentrations (up to 40% and 60% respectively), improved air quality, sequestered carbon, enhanced oxygen, negative air ionization
findings.quote: Models show that vegetating street canyon walls offers significant potential for upgrading air quality values, particularly at low wind speeds... The model predicted reductions in NO2 and PM10 concentrations of up to 40% and 60%, respectively...

findings.consequent: Reduced overall glare of cities, diffused killer beacon effect, shielded circadian well-being from city lights, nuanced/softened interior light quality, visible breezes, neurologically relevant circadian/seasonal/weather info
findings.quote: To protect night-migrating birds, three-dimensional Green Façade Systems that add a double-skin-screen of vegetation can be effective because they reduce the overall glare of cities, diffusing the killer beacon effect of each illuminated building.

findings.consequent: Engaged homeostatically effective pleasure/reward motivator, reduced anxiety and paranoia, lasting mental health improvements
findings.quote: Our body-brain associates birdsong with well-being, with freshness and springtime, and with things generally being 'ok'... Daily interactions with birds are linked to lasting mental health improvements... birdsong was found to reduce anxiety and paranoia.

findings.antecedent: Façade vegetation and air layer between plants and building wall
findings.consequent: Sound-absorbing barrier, reduced noise levels (5dB reduction -> $3.9 billion annual benefit)
findings.quote: Additionally, the combination of façade vegetation and the layer of air between plants and building wall can function as a sound-absorbing barrier... A comprehensive 2010 study found that: The sound absorption coefficient of the vertical greenery system in the reverberation chamber has one of the highest values compared with other building materials and furnishings.
